changes: Mihomo consumes a root-owned live tailnet provider file, independent of HTTP port collisions or obsolete HTTP pollers
The diagnostic HTTP listener prefers loopback port 18766 and falls back to a kernel-assigned loopback port; the dashboard reports the actual binding
Active status and heartbeat handling independently revoke approval when the protected resolver entry disappears or changes
The refresh interval and Configure link are alongside the IP-check details

validation.visual: Native dashboard scenarios and populated Settings rendered in light/dark; Direct light and active-audit Rule dark inspected at 1040x690 points with the interval beside IP-check details
validation.artifactIdentity: Installed GUI/core/helper match packaged bytes; strict ad-hoc signature verification passed
validation.providerPermissions: Live provider file is root-owned with mode 0600 inside the private mihomo directory
validation.resolverGuard: Actual resolver removal recorded mimo_dns_configuration_lost and mimo_gate_closed in the same logged second, followed by automatic Rule and MagicDNS recovery

physicalMacObservation: User-reported Rule/Allowed had no responding DNS listener and no owned system resolver. Reload profile restored TCP DNS on 1053 with the expected synthetic public A answer. Full tailnet-name resolution on that physical Mac has not yet been confirmed.
limits: The original persistent Allowed-with-missing-DNS failure was not reproduced in the VM; the new status/heartbeat guard is additional defense, not proof of the original cause
Runtime and native UI checks ran only in mimo-vm; no broad reboot, sleep, fault, multi-user or uninstall campaign repeated
Provider-port fallback does not move the DNS listener from 1053
Cross-tailnet shared nodes require full names; earlier short-name expectations were invalid and corrected
An intermediate HTTP-provider implementation contacted the occupied old port through obsolete engine pollers; the final file-provider build passed zero-requests-to-that-port checks
